summary: On Python 3.11+, cancelling a workflow with in-flight activities emits one spurious ERROR log per activity, even though cancellation works correctly. This residual from #1523's fix pollutes error logs due to stale exception callbacks armed by asyncio.shield's outer cancellation.
userImpact: Error logs are polluted with spurious ERROR messages during normal workflow cancellation, potentially triggering false alerts despite correct cancellation behavior.
rootCause: When workflow cancel occurs, asyncio.shield's _outer_done_callback arms _log_on_exception on the inner future before the except CancelledError block runs, so uncancel() cannot undo it. When the activity completes with an exception, the already-armed callback logs the orphaned exception.
proposedFix: Three possible approaches: (1) drop stale callbacks before re-shielding, (2) avoid re-shielding the same future across loop iterations, or (3) consume the orphaned exception explicitly to suppress _log_on_exception.
keyQuote: So it's exactly one residual log per cancelled in-flight activity, structurally unavoidable with the current shield-and-reshield pattern.
